findings.message: The open-attachment handler resolves the id and calls att.open(ref.path) without first checking that the file still exists. The injected opener in extension.ts runs vscode.open directly and only logs a rejected command. For an attachment that is gone from disk, the click is therefore handed to VS Code (which may show its own file-not-found editor) rather than being detected by the host, logged and dropped. ChatAttachmentDeps has no stat seam and the host makes no stat call on the resolved path.
findings.expectationRef: LLD errorPaths.errorCases — 'An attached file is gone when the turn runs or when a chip is clicked': detection 'For a click, the host's stat of the resolved path fails'; response 'A click logs and does nothing.'

findings.message: All 28 promised unit, integration and live tests are present by exact title in the changed test files (attachment-store, cli-adapter, protocol, session-file-store, render-registry, chat-panel, chat-shell, extension-chat-wiring, live-cli), but they are present but unverified: no build record is available and the suite was not run in this review, so no pass-state can be asserted.

The two promised live tests (live claude, live codex) are present but unverified: both are skip-gated on the LIVE flag and on the CLI binary being installed, so a default suite run skips them, and there is no build record showing they ran or passed.
findings.expectationRef: live claude: with the argv the adapter builds for a request with readDirs, a prompt naming an image and a text file in that directory is answered from their content; live codex: with the argv the adapter builds, a prompt naming an image and a text file in the attachments directory is answered from their content

findings.message: The two promised smoke checks have no automated test in the changed set and no build record recording that they were carried out: the manual VS Code check (paste a screenshot, attach a document, chips, answer from content, chip click opens the file) and the whole-plugin-suite run. Both are unverified, not confirmed missing — they are manual or run-level checks by nature.
findings.expectationRef: in VS Code: pasting a screenshot and attaching a document show chips, the message shows them after sending, the assistant answers from their content, and a chip click opens the file; whole plugin suite: every test passes apart from the two manifest-catalog tests that failed before this Story

findings.message: The testsReaching grounding is hollow for this Story, so the empty edges are not reported as HIGH not-exercised gaps. The graph links only named helper functions; the top-level test(...) callbacks are anonymous and carry no edges, so symbols such as safeName, dirOf, nextPath, writing, changePending, submitTurn, runTurn, handleMessage, base64Bytes, findAttachment, postPending and the claude/codex argv builders show empty testsReaching even though titled tests in attachment-store.test.ts, chat-panel.test.ts, chat-shell.test.ts and cli-adapter.test.ts target exactly that behaviour (confirmed by a title search of the test files, not by reading test bodies or running them). Per-symbol coverage therefore cannot be confirmed from the graph; running the plugin suite is the way to settle it.
findings.expectationRef: testsReaching edges for the changed symbols in attachment-store.ts, chat-panel.ts and cli-adapter.ts
